classification.difficultyReason: Infer square side and inscribed-circle radius from given area, then subtract familiar circlearea.

content.prompt: If the square in the shape has an area of $64\text{ cm}^2$, find the area of the shaded region. Give the exact answer and an approximation correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Original square with inscribed circle, mathematical four-corner shaded complement retained. Given squarearea64 stated in prompt, no derived side/radius printed.
spec.answerVisibility: Original given dimensions/marks only; no computed answers displayed.

answer.worked:
The square side is $\sqrt{64}=8\text{ cm}$, so the inscribed circle has radius 4 cm.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=64-\pi(4)^2\\A&=(64-16\pi)\text{ cm}^2\\A&\approx13.73\text{ cm}^2.\end{aligned}$$
